claims.statement: SandboxBackendProtocolV2 extends BackendProtocolV2 with shell execution and a non-empty backend identifier; BackendProtocolV2 uses structured results for reads, listings, searches, globs, writes, and optional deletion.

BaseSandbox requires concrete implementations to provide execute, uploadFiles, and downloadFiles, and implements higher-level listing, paginated text/binary reads, raw reads, literal grep, glob, writes, edits, and deletion on top of those primitives.
BaseSandbox deletion shell-quotes the requested path but executes rm -rf without confining the operation to a sandbox root, so deletion can reach anything accessible to the sandbox shell.

LocalShellBackend executes commands directly on the host with shell:true and the user's permissions; rootDir and virtualMode govern filesystem handling but virtualMode does not restrict shell commands.

LocalShellBackend creates its root directory during initialize, resets only its initialized flag on close, and its factory uploads initialFiles after initialization; command execution supports configurable environment inheritance, timeout, output truncation, stderr labeling, and timeout exit code 124.

LangSmithSandbox wraps an existing LangSmith Sandbox or creates one from exactly one of snapshotId or deprecated templateName, executes through sandbox.run with a 30-minute default timeout, and resolves its API key from the apiKey option or LANGSMITH_API_KEY.
LangSmithSandbox performs transfers through native read/write APIs with per-path results and standardized error mapping, preserves files across stop/start, and deletes the remote sandbox on close.

DaytonaSandbox initialization resolves credentials, provisions from an image or snapshot, uploads initial files, and assigns the provider sandbox ID; close deletes the remote sandbox while stop preserves a sandbox that can be started again.

DaytonaSandbox transfers files one at a time, creates parent directories before uploads, permits partial batch success, and maps provider failures to file_not_found, permission_denied, is_directory, or invalid_path; command timeouts and execution failures become structured DaytonaSandboxError codes.

Daytona authentication prefers an explicit auth.apiKey over DAYTONA_API_KEY, resolves API URL from options then DAYTONA_API_URL then a default, and resolves target from an explicit target or DAYTONA_TARGET.

DenoSandbox creates a microVM through Sandbox.create after resolving its token, supports reconnect by ID, maps deprecated memoryMb/lifetime options to memory/timeout, and closes by terminating the client-held sandbox; stop is an alias for close rather than a resumable state.

DenoSandbox executes through /bin/bash -c and translates timeouts and command failures into DenoSandboxError codes, while its current upload/download bridge converts byte arrays to text and uses writeTextFile and cat rather than preserving arbitrary binary bytes.

Deno authentication prefers a token option, then deprecated auth.token, then DENO_DEPLOY_TOKEN; the integration tests skip when credentials or sandbox-plan access are unavailable and run sequentially.

ModalSandbox initialization validates credentials, resolves an app and image, converts named volumes and secrets to SDK objects, creates the sandbox, and uploads initial files; close, terminate, and stop terminate the container rather than providing a restart operation.

ModalSandbox executes with sh -c, transfers bytes through the Modal filesystem API with relative paths normalized to absolute paths, and classifies SandboxFilesystemNotFoundError before message-based errors when producing standardized file-operation codes.

Modal credentials resolve token ID and token secret independently from explicit options or MODAL_TOKEN_ID and MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET, and its integration suite skips without both values while exercising the common suite sequentially.

VfsBackend implements BackendProtocolV2 rather than SandboxBackendProtocolV2, stores files in an in-memory VirtualFileSystem rooted at /workspace, rejects paths outside that workspace, and provides no command execution.

VfsBackend stop drops the in-memory filesystem and resets initialization, while its factory creates independent stores; its integration tests cover pagination, metadata/search/glob behavior, binary reads, path confinement, and factory independence without shell execution.

The shared sandbox standard-test harness creates one shared sandbox for most tests, uses temporary instances for lifecycle and initial-file cases, retries creation for transient failures, and covers lifecycle, execution, transfers, pagination, edits, listing, grep, glob, initial files, and workflows.

Daytona integration tests label and sweep test sandboxes and configure provider-side auto-stop/auto-delete safety intervals, while provider-specific Deno and Modal tests verify reconnect and runtime/image behavior beyond the shared suite.
